items.summary: What if the brain evolved to serve the gut? Scientists at Flinders University are challenging a cornerstone of biology, arguing that the gut's nervous system may be the body's original "brain," with the brain evolving later to support its needs.

items.title: Indonesia fires have burned nearly 2 million hectares: Monitor
items.summary: Fires in Indonesia that have caused a regional haze crisis burned through over 1.9 million hectares (4.7 million acres) between January and the end of September this year, a monitor analyzing satellite imagery said on Monday.

items.title: How bacteria survive in a world full of killer bacteriophages
items.summary: Humans throughout history have invented a variety of ways to fight back against troublesome bacteria. But bacteria live in a dangerous world too. items.title: Enigmatic Mercury will remain a puzzle until someone sends a lander
items.summary: Mercury remains one of our solar system's most elusive and difficult planets to study. It's easier to send probes to the icy moons of Saturn or Jupiter, or even to Pluto, than to land on our innermost planet, Mercury.

items.title: Alaska’s monster tsunami sent water 1,580 feet up a mountain
items.summary: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area.
